Fazhou Daoji is the exact instructor who shows Yungu Fahui the saying ‘who is it who recollects Buddha?’ while Fazhou is in seclusion at Tianning. ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Records call it a “saying” (話), say that the biography says that Fazhou Daoji showed him the saying ‘who is reciting the buddha’s name?’” (示以念佛是誰話), or command a student to “investigate ‘who is reciting the buddha’s name?’” (參念佛是誰).
EvidenceBody: One verse reverses it as “who is reciting the buddha’s name—who recites the buddha’s name?” (念佛是誰誰念佛), and another continues “who is the buddha?” (誰是佛). Wuyi Yuanlai says to “raise only one phrase” (單提一句), identifies “who” (誰) as the word in question, and compares it in that passage to a hair-cutting sword and a poison-coated drum. In a recorded interview, the student states the phrase; Juelang Daosheng replies, “who is not reciting the buddha’s name?” (不念佛是誰) and raises a ceremonial scepter. Zen thus takes vocabulary associated with buddha-name recitation and makes the literal who-question a named saying, command, biographical turning point, and public exchange. The entry reports only those recorded actions.
